chunks: Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sufi narrated to me, saying:

Al-Ma'mun said to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) one day, 'When we enter Baghdad, God willing, we will do this and that.' Then Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) told him, 'You will enter Baghdad, O Commander of the Faithful.' When I was alone with him, I said to him, 'I heard something that saddened me, and I mentioned it to him.' He said, 'O Abu Husayn, and that is how he used to nickname me by dropping the Alif and Lam, and what do I have to do with Baghdad? I will not see Baghdad, nor will Baghdad see me.'

key_terms.أَبَا حُسَيْنٍ: Abu Husayn, the kunya (nickname) of the narrator
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Rida, title of Imam Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him)
key_terms.طَرْحِ الْأَلِفِ وَاللَّامِ: Dropping the Alif and Lam, a linguistic reference to the nickname 'Al-Rida' becoming 'Rida'

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) predict about his relationship with Baghdad?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the political tension between the Abbasid Caliph Al-Ma'mun and Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.), illustrating the Imam's subtle resistance to being confined within the political center of Baghdad. The prophecy that 'he would enter Baghdad but not see it' is interpreted by Shia scholars as a metaphor for his brief, forced stay and subsequent death in Tus, emphasizing his spiritual detachment from the caliphate's worldly power. Additionally, the text notes Al-Ma'mun's affectionate nickname for the Imam, revealing the complex personal dynamics beneath the public political maneuvering.
